question: the reduced V4.1 vehicle cannot produce a matching token because its router is near-tied. The shipped checkpoint would not be. Why has it not been used?
answer: because the shipped ORACLE has never been able to run. Two named prerequisites are missing, both implementable. The checkpoint itself is present and locked.

correction.what_i_said: the V4.1 cells cannot be closed by engineering, and need 'a checkpoint whose routing is not near-tied'
correction.what_is_true: that checkpoint IS on disk -- 476 GB across 48 safetensors shards, bound by a checkpoint lock of 96,085 tensors and 510,286,023,000 bytes at ~/.cache/opentallas/deepseek-v4.1-flash/checkpoint.lock.json. The shipped ROM wafer and ROM array DEPLOYMENTS are built. What is missing is the oracle to compare against, and that is engineering, not mathematics.
correction.why_it_matters: 'cannot be closed by engineering' was the wrong summary. The reduced VEHICLE cannot be closed; the shipped path can, and has a blocker with a name and a template.

what_is_already_present.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 97,887 MiB, entirely free
what_is_already_present.oracle_tool: tools/run_deepseek_v41_reference_oracle.py, with a --stage tokens that refuses rather than pretending

the_two_blockers.requirement: a V4.1 layer-streaming engine, the analogue of runtime/reference/deepseek_v4_oracle.py::StreamingDeepSeekV4, that materialises one block and one routed expert at a time from the 48 released shards
the_two_blockers.template: runtime/reference/deepseek_v4_oracle.py, 1,337 lines, with a WeightStore that holds lazy safetensors handles and materialises host/device tensors on demand. The V4.1 analogue additionally has to cover hyper-connections, the compressor, the indexer and Engram.
the_two_blockers.why_it_is_needed: 510 GB of weights against 188 GB of host RAM and 98 GB of device memory. The V4-Flash oracle read 201 GB with a PEAK DEVICE FOOTPRINT OF 361 MB by streaming, which is the proof the approach works at this scale.

the_two_blockers.requirement: a residency policy for the two Engram tables (202.76 GB) that ParallelEngramEmbedding.forward's F.embedding over the whole table can be served from
the_two_blockers.note: F.embedding only reads the rows it indexes, so a row-gather against memory-mapped shards is the shape of the answer rather than a full materialisation. Not yet written.

what_this_does_not_change: the reduced vehicle's divergence is still fully explained and still not closable: 0.82% at layer 0 moves the token, the MoE's discontinuity supplies that amplification from sub-ulp inputs, and neither fp32 split is more accurate than the other
the three reduced V4.1 cells still execute end to end under the real control plane, and the wafer and array still agree exactly on token 1126
not_a_claim: that the shipped cells WILL close once the oracle runs. A trained router has decisive margins, which is why the V4-Flash cells close, but that is an expectation and not a measurement until the oracle exists
that the streaming engine is a small job: the V4 template is 1,337 lines and V4.1 has four subsystems V4 does not
